shardNotes: Read 2026-10-06 by the Round 1036 championship research agent. Every season is England tier 2 and has 24 clubs, checked against the row count of every source.

Sources: 1990-91 to 2007-08 rsssf.org/engpaul season pages; 2008-09 to 2025-26 rsssf.org/tablese pages (eng09 is 2008-09, engYYYY is the season ending in YYYY). ESPN standings (the JSON behind espn.com/soccer/standings/_/league/ENG.2/season/Y, season Y = Y-(Y+1)) from 2002-03, the first season ESPN has. 1990-91 to 2001-02 have no second source on the brief list (worldfootball.net refuses automated reads with HTTP 402 and 403, statscrew.com has no English tables, ESPN starts 2002-03), so those seasons carry two further independent non-wiki archives, footballsite.co.uk and englishfootballleaguetables.co.uk, marked listed:false. englishfootballleaguetables.co.uk is also the third source that settles 2002-03 and 2003-04.
printed holds each club as each source prints it, in the order of sources. RSSSF engpaul prints promoted and relegated clubs in capitals; that is kept as printed.

Names are matched across sources by an explicit alias list only (Wolves, Wolverhampton W, QPR, Queen's Park Rangers, AFC Bournemouth, Brighton and similar), never fuzzily. Season scoped aliases, each explained in that season's note: 2002-03 RSSSF misspellings Crystal Palalce and Sheffield Wedsnesday; 2002-03 and 2003-04 ESPN printing Wimbledon FC as Milton Keynes Dons.

canon is the club's spelling in src/lib/soccerCareerEngine.ts HAND_CLUBS or src/data/soccerCareerClubPool.ts (England and Wales), matched by exact club identity: Manchester City is Man City, Newcastle United is Newcastle, West Bromwich Albion is West Brom, Queens Park Rangers is QPR, Brighton and Hove Albion is Brighton, Wolverhampton Wanderers is Wolves, West Ham United is West Ham, AFC Bournemouth is Bournemouth. Clubs the career world does not know (Leicester City, Sheffield Wednesday, Wimbledon, Milton Keynes Dons and others) have canon null. Sheffield Wednesday is never Sheffield United; Bristol Rovers is never Bristol City.
pos is the final league position when every source prints the same one; it did in all 36 seasons. Play-off winners keep their league position (for example 3 to 6).

Self check: 36 seasons, each 24 clubs with no duplicate and positions 1 to 24; every source agrees on membership; 35 season to season transitions checked against the RSSSF tier 1 and tier 3 tables: every club leaving tier 2 is in tier 1 (from positions 1 to 6) or tier 3 (from positions 21 to 24) the next season, every club arriving was in tier 1 or tier 3 the season before, and leavers equal arrivals. 1990-91 promoted four (top flight grew to 22) and 1994-95 relegated four (top flight shrank to 20), both as printed.

seasons.note: Only one source here (rsssf.org) is on the brief's named list: worldfootball.net refused automated reads (HTTP 402 and 403), statscrew.com carries no English league tables, and ESPN's standings start at 2002-03. Two further independent non-wiki archives (footballsite.co.uk, englishfootballleaguetables.co.uk) agree with RSSSF on all 24 clubs and every position.
seasons.ruling: Lead ruling 2026-10-06: the data law asks for two independent non-wiki sources; the brief's host list was examples, not a closed list. 11v11.com (Association of Football Statisticians data), footballsite.co.uk and englishfootballleaguetables.co.uk are independent of RSSSF and are accepted as the second source.
